posts.title: Fake bank alerts stealing login details
posts.sms: Dear customer, your bank app is locked. Click bit.ly/bank-update to verify your PIN immediately.
tips: Banks never send SMS links asking for your secret PIN.
Call your bank using the official phone number on your card.
Never share a one-time login code with anyone.
posts.message: Banks warn that fraudsters use fake SMS links to steal mobile banking passwords and empty accounts.
posts.action: Forward suspicious scam SMS text messages for free to 333
posts.caption:
Banks are warning customers about fraudsters sending fake app update links by SMS. Never click unknown links or share your secret PIN, Daily Nation reports.

Have you received a fake bank alert lately?

#Usiibiwe #KenyaOnRecord
beats: Banks in Kenya warn that *fake SMS alerts* target mobile accounts.
Scammers send links that mimic official mobile banking login pages.
A real bank will never ask for your *secret PIN*.
Have you received a fake bank SMS on your phone?

scripts.radio:
Good evening. This is Kenya on Record, bringing you the facts that matter to your pocket and your community.

First, your savings. Commercial banks have issued an urgent warning against SMS phishing scams. Con artists are circulating text messages claiming your account is blocked or requires verification, accompanied by a link. Clicking that link directs you to a duplicate webpage designed to steal your mobile banking credentials. Remember: no legitimate bank will ever send you an SMS link asking for your PIN or password. If you receive one, delete it and contact your branch directly.

On public health and industry, plans are underway for a dedicated biopharma park at Konza Technopolis. The goal is to manufacture essential medicines locally. For decades, Kenyans have borne the burden of expensive imported medicine and fragile supply chains. If executed properly, local manufacturing will lower treatment costs significantly. However, accountability is key. Citizens must track these timelines and public investments to ensure this vision delivers affordable medicine rather than another delayed project.

Finally, we honour Lamu Old Town, which has preserved over seven centuries of Swahili architecture and continuous community living. It is a vital reminder that national development must respect and preserve our cultural heritage.

Kwa ufupi: Benki hazitumi viungo vya SMS kuomba nenosiri au PIN yako; ukipokea ujumbe kama huo, usibonyeze. Kule Konza, mpango wa kutengeneza dawa humu nchini unalenga kushusha gharama za matibabu, huku Lamu ikisherehekea zaidi ya miaka mia saba ya kuhifadhi utamaduni wetu wa Waswahili.

I am your host. Stay informed, and stay vigilant.
scripts.voice_note:
Habari zenu. Here is your weekly briefing from Kenya on Record.

First, please warn your family and friends about bank SMS scams. Fraudsters are sending texts claiming your bank account has issues, with a link to resolve it. That link is designed to steal your passwords and drain your funds. No genuine bank will text you a link asking for your PIN or login details. Do not click; just call your branch.

Second, Konza Technopolis is planning a biopharma park to manufacture essential medicines locally. Most of our drugs are imported, making healthcare painfully expensive. Producing them locally could bring down prescription costs, but we must keep our eyes on the implementation so public funds yield real results.

Lastly, a nod to Lamu Old Town, which has preserved over seven hundred years of Swahili architecture and community life. Modern progress should never erase who we are.

Share this voice note to keep someone informed today.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Banks will never SMS you links asking for passwords or PINs. Do not click links claiming your account is blocked. Delete them and call your bank.
scripts.reels: Kenyans spend billions every year on imported essential medicines, leaving families stranded by high pharmacy bills. The planned biopharma manufacturing park at Konza Technopolis aims to change that by producing critical drugs locally. Homegrown manufacturing means lower prices, reliable supply, and healthcare that ordinary citizens can actually afford. But ambitious master plans don't cure illness—actual delivery does. We must hold officials accountable to ensure this investment delivers real medicine to public shelves, on time.
